newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-AC MILAN'S BAGGIO WON'T RULE OUT TRANSFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AC MILAN'S BAGGIO WON'T RULE OUT TRANSFER.

text.p: Former World Cup star Roberto Baggio, reported to be planning to leave AC Milan after falling out with coach Arrigo Sacchi, did not rule it out on Saturday.
"Now more than ever I do not exclude any possibilities, even going to Inter. It is one of many (options)," Baggio told reporters as he left Milan's camp.

He was responding to a report in the Corriere dello Sport daily that he had argued with Sacchi, who resigned as Italy's national coach two weeks ago to return to his old club AC Milan, and was planning to leave.
The newspaper's front-page headline read: "Baggio Breaks with Sacchi". An inside headline said: "Baggio to Sacchi: 'Enough! I'm Off'.".

Baggio, who is suffering from sciatica, told reporters: "Right now I want to concentrate on getting better and, most importantly, I want to take a few days to think about what to do so I haven't yet spoken to (AC Milan owner Silvio) Berlusconi".
Nicknamed "The Divine Ponytail" by fans, Baggio joined Milan at the beginning of last season from Juventus where he helped the Turin club win the league title.
He was injured much of last season.

After missing a penalty in the 1994 World Cup final in Los Angeles against Brazil, Baggio played for Italy only sporadically until Sacchi dropped him from the squad for a European championship last May.
Corriere dello Sport speculated in its report that bad feelings between Baggio and Sacchi stemmed from the missed penalty.
Sacchi, who helped Milan win the European Cup twice when he was coach there before joining the national team, returned to Milan last week as coach after suddenly resigning his Italy job.
He replaced Uruguayan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez, who handed in his notice after Milan had slumped to ninth in the league and had been dumped out of the Italian Cup by Vicenza.
Baggio, who comes from Vicenza, played in that match.
Milan, reigning Italian champions, have had a disastrous start to the season and are now seventh in serie A. They travel to bottom club Reggiana on Sunday where Baggio is not expected to play.
